newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Avmin says to sign Konkola agreement soon.
newsitem.headline: Avmin says to sign Konkola agreement soon.

text.p: Avmin Ltd is due to sign an option agreement on the development of Zambia's Konkola North mine soon, the company said on Monday.
"Avmin is due to sign the agreement shortly," a company spokesman said.

The development of the Konkola ore body on the Zambian Copperbelt is seen as crucial to the future of Zambia's copper industry as reserves at the main Nchanga open pit will run out by the end of the century.

A consortium led by Zambia Copper Investments Ltd, a subsidiary of mining giant Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, last week signed an agreement with the Zambian government to develop the Konkola Deep mine.

Avmin said last year it was targeting to delineate ore resources at Konkola North of not less than 100 million tonnes at copper grade "adequate to support the economic exploitation of ore at depths of up to 1,500 metres".
Zambia's privatisation agency said last year the deal with Avmin should be signed this month and that a decision on the development of the mine can be made within the next five years.
Avmin is the minerals division of South African mining house Anglovaal Ltd.
